ranking.why: The patient's symptoms of cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and bilateral lower extremity edema, along with the presence of a patent foramen ovale and right-to-left shunt, are consistent with Eisenmenger Syndrome, as described in the reference material.

The patient's symptoms of exertional dyspnea, fatigue, and shortness of breath, along with the elevated pulmonary artery pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy, are consistent with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension, as described in the reference material.

While the patient's symptoms are consistent with Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension, the reference material does not provide sufficient information to distinguish it from other forms of Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.

The patient's symptoms of shortness of breath, fatigue, and exertional dyspnea, along with the elevated pulmonary artery pressure, are consistent with Pulmonary Hypertension, as described in the reference material.
